When the only information about a phase diagram is a graphical representation and this image is captured digitally, calibration of pixel location with a composition and temperature pair according to the given axes is possible. In this way, the extracted boundary pixels can then be used to translate the original graph into discrete quantities. Since most images may consist of a line thickness greater than one pixel and there is uncertainty in the calibration, these input points are then fitted according to common forms. The model form, while providing a well-fit dataset should not be taken as truly indicative of underlying thermodynamics.
